title: Experiment: per-vector unit pricing + batch discounts for embeddings & rerank; QSA and enterprise contract prep
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: define and validate a per-vector unit pricing model for embeddings and reranking with time-limited batch discount promotions, and address enterprise QSA/contract language implications. Deliverables: experimental pricing tiers, billing metrics instrumentation, customer-facing pricing page draft, and completed QSA responses for legal and sales enablement.
acceptance_criteria: A/B experiment plan with sample sizes and success criteria documented
Instrumentation emits per-vector and per-batch revenue metrics to billing dashboard
Prototype price ladder and discount rules implemented in billing simulator
At least two existing enterprise customers briefed and consent to pilot terms
QSA draft completed and signed off by Security and Legal
Playbook for rollout and rollback documented
comments: 2026-02-10 — Ticket created by Asha Patel: initial scope and hypothesis: moving from per-call to per-vector unit reduces pricing opacity and improves unit economics for high-density use cases; batch discounts to encourage behind-the-scenes batching.

2026-02-15 — Design review with Growth and Billing: trade-off: higher cognitive load on customers vs clear cost predictability for heavy embedding users. Agreed to provide calculator and per-request estimates in the Console.

2026-02-22 — Engineering sync (ENG-2104): agreed instrumentation changes required: add 'vectors_consumed' and 'batches_aggregated' fields to usage events. Dependency raised to ENG-2104 for metrics pipeline work.

2026-03-01 — Experiment plan posted in Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PR/pages/Vector+Pricing+Experiment (internal). Includes A/B test design, 12-week rollout, KPIs: ARPU per heavy user, churn delta, average cost per 1M vectors.

2026-03-05 — Legal & Security kickoff: QSA implications noted: per-vector billing does not change data flows but affects billing descriptors and audit logs. Action: produce QSA table mapping pricing telemetry to billing artifacts. Owner: Legal (S. Moreno).

2026-03-07 — Pricing mockups shared with Sales: Google Drive doc with sample contract language and pilot discounts: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/pricing-pilot-embeddings. Sales feedback: emphasize predictability for contract negotiations; request a 'cap' mechanism for enterprise pilots.
2026-03-09 — Billing simulator PR opened: github.com/redwood/billing/pull/421 — implements simulator for pricing ladder and batch discounts. Requesting Engineering review from @eliot-ramos.

2026-03-11 — Security review draft attached to Confluence QSA page. Pending Legal signoff. Noted additional requirement: audit trail for batched aggregation decisions and customer-facing explanations for any retroactive cost adjustments.

2026-03-12 — PM decision: proceed with two parallel experiments: (A) per-vector unit with staged batch-discount thresholds; (B) volume slab pricing (control). Launch date targeted 2026-03-30 for internal pilot with 3 enterprise customers. Next steps: finalize billing telemetry, complete QSA matrix, legal to prepare pilot contract addendum.
notes: Spike concluded: model simulation indicates ~12-18% reduction in cost-per-effective-query for customers that can batch aggressively; customers with single-shot requests see marginal change.
Sales proposed a temporary 'pilot cap' that limits monthly spend exposure. Finance requested revenue forecasting model for 12-month horizon before broader rollout.
